newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest seen mostly dry through next week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest seen mostly dry through next week.

text.p: A series of cold fronts were expected to push across the U.S. Midwest over the next week but rainfall amounts were likely to be minimal, forecasters said.
"We still are going to be looking at relatively dry conditions for harvest over the next week or so," said Mike Palmerino, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
Rainfall amounts were expected to total less than .25 inch with coverage near 50 percent across the U.S. Midwest, Palmerino said.
A cold front was expected to move across the western and central corn belt Thursday and Friday, reaching the eastern corn belt by Saturday, said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster with Weather Express.

Below freezing temperatures were possible in parts of Minnesota, Wisconsin and Iowa Thursday morning. Rainfall amounts of up to .25 inch were possible but Gesser forecast coverage of less than 20 percent.
"That system does not look like much of a rain producer," he said. "What you're looking at is below normal precipitation over the next week to 10 days."

Long-range forecasts indicated another cold front early next week with below freezing temperatures possible across the northern and central Midwest, said Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis.
"We may be seeing some sharply colder temperatures next week," Solberg said.
Little rainfall was expected with that front, he added.
Palmerino said the front could bring "the coldest weather of the season so far" with the lowest readings expected Monday and Tuesday.
